review_reference: Owner decisions in chat by D-Eminence. 0107 (OCR page allowance, fair claim and AI usage): 2026-11-02/03 (Migrate item 7) "allowance 500 pages/facility/month (Textract+AI), only super admin raises, 100% pauses reading but not review/manual entry"; 2026-11-04 (about 23:55 UTC) "Lift hold, US only": the OCR AI reading ships with Claude processing in the United States only (inference_geo us, OCR_AI_US_PROCESSING_APPROVED), superseding the Q33 A hold on this PR. Numbered 0107, the next free number after production's 0106. Signed: the owner approved this release in chat on 2026-11-05 (about 00:52 UTC) with "approve 0107".
evidence: Single migration 0107_ocr_page_allowance.sql (OCR page allowance, fair claim and AI usage) and runtime-grants.sql's 0107 block, signed by the owner (see review_reference). NUMBER: drafted as 0110 on 0103 and renumbered 0107, the next free number after staging's 0106 (coordinator decision: numbers follow release order; OCR goes before patient chat part 2; verify-release-contract refuses a gap); only its number in messages, comments and the temporary table name changed, plus the three changes below that 0104-0106 called for. It applies after 0106. What it needs from them: ocr.claim_worker_job exactly as 0105 left it (md5 25b7ebb837fc93a4af52e555ffdac576, the only accepted body; the fair claim copies it), so 0105 must be applied; on a 0104 database it stops with nothing applied (md5 mismatch). Every other pinned body was re-measured on a fresh 0001-0106 database and is unchanged (0104 replaces only identity.has_active_consent_grant, 0105 only ocr.claim_worker_job, 0106 inserts two rows); nothing 0104 or 0106 adds is read. Changes for 0104-0106: (1) the pin of ocr.claim_worker_job renewed to 0105's body; (2) the fair claim returns, as 0105's claim does, the detected media type of the clean scan bound to the job's source version and SHA-256 (0105's owner decision D3), not the declared type (the worker claims only through the fair claim); (3) review finding: ocr.pause_worker_job_for_allowance now takes the facility's page-limit lock, pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('hid.ocr.page-limit:' || facility_id, 0)), the same key ocr.set_facility_page_limit takes, before it reads the allowance, so a raise above use racing a pause never leaves the job parked (the pause either sees the new limit and answers NULL, or parks first and the waiting raise resumes it). Backward compatible: three new tables and nine new functions in schema ocr, one more allowed transition in the existing trigger function ocr.validate_job_write (CREATE OR REPLACE; signature, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path, volatility, owner and ACL kept; md5 e9ea263ec9f29355eb9a6a81fd2d7b37 before, 58ff61a5b9b95685f6a6d3f938b8481f after), no other table, column, constraint, policy, trigger or function change (ocr.claim_worker_job keeps 0105's body, checked again after), no row touched. Today's ocr-api, ocr-worker and identity-api images run unchanged. WHAT IT DOES. ocr.facility_page_limits (facility_id pk -> identity.facilities, pages_limit 1-100000, set_by_account_id, reason 1-240, set_at), ocr.page_usage (job_id pk; facility_id -> identity.facilities; usage_month = first day of the Africa/Lagos month of the first recording; pages 1-200; recorded_at) and ocr.ai_usage (primary key (job_id, attempt_no, model); model ^claude-[a-z0-9-]+$ at most 100 characters; facility_id -> identity.facilities; usage_month as page_usage; requests integer and input, output, cache read, cache write tokens bigint, all >= 0; recorded_at): no foreign key from either usage table to ocr.jobs, so the counts outlive the 24-hour working data and never block its deletion; row-level security forced, one policy for the OCR functions' owner, no grant to any runtime role, no patient or page text. Commands (SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pinned starting pg_catalog, ocr, owned by the owner of ocr.jobs): ocr.worker_page_allowance(uuid,uuid), ocr.record_worker_pages(uuid,uuid,integer,text), ocr.pause_worker_job_for_allowance(uuid,uuid,text), ocr.claim_worker_job_fair(text,integer,integer) and ocr.record_worker_ai_usage(uuid,uuid,text,integer,bigint,bigint,bigint,bigint,text) for hid_ocr_worker only; ocr.facility_page_allowance(uuid) and ocr.facility_ocr_usage(uuid,date) for hid_ocr_runtime (inherited by hid_ocr_api_runtime) and hid_identity_runtime (staff of that facility holding ocr.job.read via auth.membership_has_permission, or a platform session with platform.admin.access; the authorization is coalesced to false so a partial session is refused); ocr.set_facility_page_limit(uuid,integer,text) for hid_identity_runtime, platform_super_admin ONLY (coordinator decision: a cost decision; platform_admin, support admins and the facility read only), in a platform session with platform.admin.access, a correlation id and healthcare-operations; upsert; platform audit row admin.ocr.page-limit.set that 0064's rules accept; above use it makes the facility's parked queued jobs due now. The fair claim copies ocr.claim_worker_job's authorization, validation (plus a NULL lease and a cap outside 1-16 refused 22023), lease recovery, eligibility and result as 0105 left them (media_type the clean scan's detected type; #variable_conflict use_column in the body; md5 49b95651106e0aaa6f8bf6c8adcdb696 checked after); it skips a facility with at least the cap of jobs processing under an unexpired lease (any provider), orders by that count, next_attempt_at, queued_at, id, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and takes the candidate's facility with pg_try_advisory_xact_lock (never waits) and counts again after it, so the cap is exact among fair claimers; claims through the unchanged ocr.claim_worker_job take no such lock. ocr.record_worker_ai_usage: fail_worker_job's claim checks, model and counts checked (22023), one row per (job, current attempt, model) whose totals the call replaces, audit ocr.worker.ai_usage_recorded (attempt, model, counts) only when something changed. ocr.facility_ocr_usage: one row per model plus one row textract with the month's pages (tokens 0, always present), for the Lagos month containing the date (NULL this month). The trigger transition: a queued job whose last_error_code IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OCR_PAGE_ALLOWANCE_USED_UP (a NULL code never qualifies; with = it did, through three-valued logic, and the new suite case caught it) may move next_attempt_at earlier, not before now - 1 minute, with the next version and optionally a new correlation id, every other column unchanged. runtime-grants.sql's 0107 block (after 0105's; 0106 changes no grant) makes exactly the grants the migration makes (USAGE on schema ocr to hid_ocr_worker, hid_ocr_runtime, hid_identity_runtime; the EXECUTE grants above; revokes from PUBLIC on the nine functions and three tables). PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): ocr.jobs, identity.facilities, auth.accounts, audit.events present; none of 0107's objects (tables, the nine functions) and validate_job_write not already this file's body; md5 of ocr.validate_job_write, ocr.fail_worker_job, ocr.claim_worker_job (the body 0105 gave it), ocr.record_job_event, the six platform session helpers, auth.account_id_for_subject, auth.account_has_active_role, auth.account_has_platform_permission, auth.membership_has_permission, identity.has_active_membership, audit.authorize_platform_event; the trigger function's attributes; the two ocr.jobs triggers; 0064's three audit constraints and authority trigger; the four runtime roles where they exist (not superuser, not BYPASSRLS; on a fresh database the role bootstrap creates them after the migrations) and hid_ocr_api_runtime inheriting hid_ocr_runtime when both exist; the permissions ocr.job.read, platform.admin.access and the roles ocr_worker, platform_super_admin; one owner for ocr.jobs and the worker commands, which may create in schema ocr; the applier is it or a member that inherits it and may SET ROLE to it. POST-CHECKS: both bodies by md5, claim_worker_job still an accepted body, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path and owner of the eight commands, the shared reckoning SECURITY INVOKER, EXECUTE exactly as granted, the three tables' owner, forced row-level security, one policy and no other privilege, no foreign key from the usage tables to ocr.jobs. LOCKS: beyond ACCESS SHARE only the new tables, the session's temporary objects and SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.facilities (three foreign keys); no index or constraint is added to ocr.jobs. PROVED for 0107 on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 with pgvector (clusters created and deleted): FRESH install of all 108 files 0001-0107 with the migrations before the role bootstrap (0 runtime roles before; plan 108 pending, dry run rolled back, apply, 0 pending), role bootstrap and --verify-only pass, the file again answers '0107: already applied', all 81 database suites pass (the new suite 180 cases). UPGRADE from 0106: a database built by staging 50089e90's own runner, files and runtime-grants.sql (107 files, ledger last 0106, hid:staging:ocr-worker seeded, 1210 non-owner grants; the new suite fails there), plan 1 pending (0107 with this sha256), dry run rolled back with no 0107 object, apply, 0 pending, the runner again applies nothing, the file again answers '0107: already applied'; 1221 non-owner grants after the migration and after a bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql (the same as the fresh install), the 0107 ACLs after the migration equal those after the bootstrap and those of the fresh install up to grantee order; all 81 suites pass. RACE (two sessions on committed copies of the suite's fixtures, clinic at 500 of 500, fresh and upgraded databases): a raise to 1000 holding its transaction while a pause runs: the pause waits about 2 s for the raise, then sees the new limit and answers NULL (the job stays processing); a pause holding its transaction while a raise runs: the raise waits, then resumes the parked job (due now). The same harness with the lock removed from the pause (a mutant) leaves the job parked until resets_on under a limit of 1000 in both orders, and the suite's lock case fails on it; a mutant fair claim returning the declared type fails the suite's media type case. services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs passed with a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds, baseline 107 files with staging 50089e90's runtime-grants.sql, 108 integrated, declared exactly 0107; dry run rolled back, checksums kept, migration grants match runtime-grants.sql (2480), 185 row-security settings unchanged), so 0105's claim has the pinned md5 on the RDS bodies too. On the 0110 draft (0103 base) the earlier proofs stand: fresh install 0001-0103 and 0110 (105 files) with the migrations before the role bootstrap, 0 pending after, role bootstrap and verification pass, all 78 database suites pass; upgrade of a 0103 database by the runner (plan 1 pending, dry run rolled back, apply, 0 pending; the file again answers '0110: already applied' and the runner applies nothing), the 0110 grants made by the migration equal those after a role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql (ACLs identical up to grantee order) and those of the fresh install; all 78 suites pass; the new suite fails on 0103. services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs passed with a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds, 104 baseline, 105 integrated; migration grants match runtime-grants.sql (2476); 185 row-security settings unchanged). Under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner (rds bodies) 0110 applies and the new suite passes in its non-bypass mode (157 cases; worker commands answer 55000 and the fair claim claims nothing, as every OCR worker command there). Negative copies stop with nothing applied: ocr.ai_usage, claim_worker_job_fair, facility_ocr_usage or record_worker_ai_usage already present ('already applied'), a changed ocr.claim_worker_job body (md5 mismatch). Concurrency: 12-16 concurrent fair claimers on two facilities with 30 and 10 queued jobs, 6 claims each with random hold times, end with exactly the cap processing per facility for caps 1, 2 and 3 (5 of 5 repeated runs at cap 2); the same harness with the advisory lock and recount removed ends with 4-8 per facility at cap 2. Mutants: 20 of 20 killed (trigger: = instead of IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, same time, no lower bound, attempt_count free; limit: platform_admin allowed; fair: no cap at all, no least-busy ordering, expired leases counted, only this provider counted, caps 0/17 accepted, no lease recovery; AI usage: no replace, no model check, replay audits, another worker's job; usage: AI month ignored, pages month ignored, no ocr.job.read, another facility, malformed rows); removing only the candidate-query cap or only the post-lock recount is not visible in one session (each layer alone holds the cap there) and the concurrency harness covers the recount.
